sentences.text: UV will still penetrate thin clouds - so even if you don't think it's that sunny, you can still burn." Yes, according to Dr Shergill.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "The skin may look darker, but it doesn’t always behave that way from a protection point of view  – because there are more genes at play than we think about," he says.

sentences.text: "I have, for example, seen South Asian people with skin cancer and I have seen people with dual-heritage get skin cancer." The broader risks of eye damage and harmful effects on the immune system from too much UV radiation affect people of all skin colour.

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: The NHS is rolling out the self-testing kits to increase screening numbers, with data suggesting about a third of women are not up to date with appointments.

sentences.text: HPV is a common virus and some high-risk types can cause changes to cells in the cervix, which can develop into cervical cancer.

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Schools had been expected to fund some of the 3.5% teachers pay increase for the current school year out of their existing budgets, which National Education Union (NEU) leaders had strongly objected to.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Daniel Kebede, the general secretary of the NEU, said the offer of more funding was a "significant" step in negotiations.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In a letter to the union on Wednesday, which has been seen by the BBC, the government said the increase would be funded by savings in employers' contributions to the local government pension scheme.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The letter said the 4.9 percentage point drop in what employers are expected to contribute will deliver "significant savings" on the pay bill for support staff, which will not be clawed back by central government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The National Education Union said it expected the extra money to be around £500m, which schools can now use towards teachers' pay this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In July, ministers accepted the recommendation of the independent pay review body for teachers and agreed a 3.5% increase from September 2026 would be followed by 3% the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The pay increase had been partly funded by an additional £700m for 2026-27 and £1.1bn for the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Independent economists at the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said that left schools facing a shortfall of around 1% between rising costs and funding this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Luke Sibieta, IFS research fellow, said the extra money would mean the pay increase this year was fully funded - and on top of other funding increases, schools would be £1.6bn better off by next year than they had expected this summer.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The additional money could potentially bring the uplift for this year into line with next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Kebede said schools has been "running on empty" and the funding signalled "a welcome return to reality, and a message of hope for the entire school community".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Headteachers, said the decision is "certainly welcome", putting schools in a "better position".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: He said his union would look carefully at the detail "to determine whether this means the pay uplift is genuinely fully funded" for schools.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said he was "pleased" at the announcement of additional funding but "the wider pressure on school and college budgets remains intense".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Similarly, the NASUWT union welcomed the news.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: General secretary Matt Wrack added schools needed "a sustainable, long-term injection of extra funding" to meet the needs of young people.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In an indicative ballot by the NEU in April, 90% of teachers who voted said they would be prepared to take industrial action over funding and pay, on a turnout of 48%.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: A formal ballot was due to begin on 3 October and close 15 December, raising the prospects of teachers pay strikes early in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The national executive of the NEU will meet on 24 September to consider whether to call that off following the additional funding on offer from the government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The marina said there were limited options available for disposal sites A wildlife trust has called for a new offshore disposal site to be found for sediment dredged from Brighton Marina, saying it remains concerned about plans being explored off Newhaven.

sentences.text: Brighton Marina has been looking for a long-term disposal site since Sussex Wildlife Trust successfully challenged a licence in 2025 for disposal of sediment at Rottingdean.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: The marina has said dredging is needed to maintain safe access and there are limited options available for disposal sites.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Sussex Wildlife Trust said Newhaven was a "protected area" that sat adjacent to the Beachy Head West Marine Conservation Zone (MCZ).
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Campaigners previously claimed the silt was a " black, thick, slimy, petrochemically smelling sludge ", but Premier Marinas, which owns Brighton Marina, said dredged silt was regularly sampled to confirm it was not harmful.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Protesters opposed the use of Rottingdean in a demo by the marina in January 2025 John Cervenka, Premier Marinas chief operating officer, said: "Maintaining safe navigational access to Brighton Marina is not optional.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: It is a legal requirement and fundamental to the operation of the marina." He said the marina was a major centre of economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: According to the marina, about 150 businesses depend on the site, creating jobs for about 1,200 people, with more than eight million visits each year.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Premier Marinas said Newhaven had been identified as a potential alternative by Sussex Wildlife Trust.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: "Our preferred option is a new offshore disposal site, well away from the MCZ." The trust said that Newhaven was already used for dredge disposal by Newhaven Port, and there was currently no available data on the impacts of additional disposal there.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Until it saw further evidence, it did not have a view on whether Newhaven was suitable, it added.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: "We will respond to any future licence application based on the ecological evidence it contains," it said.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Brighton Marina hopes to submit a marine licence application to the Marine Management Organisation in November.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: If approved, maintenance dredging could restart next spring.

sentences.text: India's government says 56 glacial lakes had been classified as "very high risk" The Himalayas are approaching a dangerous threshold as glaciers melt faster, glacial lakes grow more unstable and the mountains face a widening gap in monitoring, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The findings come in the aftermath of devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, which killed more than 1,300 people and caused widespread destruction, highlighting the growing risks from a rapidly changing Himalayan environment.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Yet only about 21 of the estimated 40,000 glaciers across the Himalaya-Karakoram region are being monitored in detail and on a sustained basis, according to the report.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: That monitoring gap matters because the physical landscape is changing rapidly.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: As glaciers retreat, they can leave behind expanding lakes held back by unstable deposits of rock and ice.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: At the same time, warming is destabilising permafrost - permanently frozen ground that can thaw as temperatures rise - and high mountain slopes, increasing the possibility of cascading hazards, the report says.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: A glacial lake outburst in 2023 triggered a flash flood, causing extensive damage in Sikkim India already has evidence of the scale of the risk.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Some 18% of Indian land is Himalayan, yet the region accounts for about 35% of disasters, according to the report.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The government told parliament in July that 56 glacial lakes had been classified as "very high risk" , external following a 2025 scientific assessment of 189 high-risk lakes in the Indian Himalayan region.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Central Water Commission is monitoring 2,485 glacial lakes larger than 10 hectares across India's Himalayan river basins, the government said.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Himalayas have already seen devastating examples of what can happen when glacial lakes burst their natural dams.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: In 2023, a glacial lake outburst flood in Sikkim killed at least 70 people and caused widespread damage to roads, bridges and hydropower projects.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: In 2021, a similar disaster in Uttarakhand killed more than 200 people after a massive flood swept through the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga valleys.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: But the danger is not confined to spectacular floods.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Himalayas are a vast natural water system feeding rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people across South Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: ICIMOD says "peak water" , external is expected around mid-century in most Hindu Kush Himalayan river basins - the point at which glacier runoff reaches its maximum before declining as glaciers lose mass.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The new research puts an unusually large economic number on that dependency.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: It estimates that Himalayan water underpins roughly 20% of India's GDP, sustaining wheat, rice, tea, hydropower and pilgrimage economies.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Yet the mountain states capture only about 5% of that value, it says.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "The Himalayas are the Third Pole," said economist Lord Nicholas Stern, chair of the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Unlike the Arctic or Antarctic, this pole has hundreds of millions of people living beneath it." The Indian Himalayan region receives roughly 400 million visits a year "This is national and international infrastructure," he said, warning that the ecological system underpinning it is "approaching a tipping point".
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Not all the forces driving glacier loss are beyond the region's control.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Systemiq research estimates that roughly a third of Himalayan glacier melt is driven by black carbon, much of it originating from brick kilns in the plains.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Soot deposited on snow and ice absorbs more sunlight and accelerates melting.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Unlike global greenhouse-gas emissions, black-carbon pollution is a lever that India and its neighbours can act on directly, the report argues.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "The Himalayas are approaching a tipping point, with millions of lives and livelihoods hanging in the balance," said Arushi Chopra, Systemiq's senior director and lead author.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Glaciers are melting faster than they were a decade ago." The report proposes 10 priority transitions, ranging from reducing black-carbon emissions and expanding glacier monitoring to improving disaster early-warning systems and changing the way tourism is developed in the mountains.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: One priority is to strengthen disaster preparedness, with governments agreeing in advance what action to take when hazards emerge - from evacuation to protecting vulnerable infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Another is to rethink tourism.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Indian Himalayan region receives roughly 400 million tourist visits a year, according to the report, and researchers argue that the objective should shift from maximising visitor numbers towards generating value that is retained and reinvested locally.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Pema Gyamtsho, director general of ICIMOD, said the risks were becoming increasingly complex.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Glaciers are retreating, permafrost and high-mountain slopes are becoming increasingly unstable, and communities and infrastructure downstream face growing risks from complex and cascading hazards," he said.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: And those risks do not stop at the borders drawn across the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Such hazards, Gyamtsho said, "do not respect national borders, and no single country can address them alone".
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: That makes cross-border monitoring, shared risk information and early-warning systems, and joint investment in resilience increasingly urgent - not just to save lives, but to protect the livelihoods and economies of hundreds of millions of people who depend on the mountains.

sentences.text: Professor Dave Chadwick from Bangor University sampling damaged remains following wildfires at Mynydd Llangynidr in Bannau Brycheiniog Scientists investigating the damage caused by severe wildfires across Wales this summer say the impact has been "catastrophic".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Extreme heat and exceptionally dry conditions throughout July and August left landscapes such as heathland, moorland and upland grasslands vulnerable to fast spreading fires, resulting in one of the UK's worst wildfire seasons in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones, who is leading a Bangor University survey of several sites across Wales, said the scale of damage was far greater than what was immediately visible.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet," said Jones.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: During the July peak, fires affected approximately 2,760 acres of countryside across north Wales alone, the equivalent of more than 1,500 football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: At Sychnant Pass in Conwy county, one of the most significant blazes saw 36 homes having to be evacuated and about 200 acres of land affected.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones said the scale of damage from the wildfires was far greater than what was immediately visible At Sychnant Pass today, there are slight green shoots of recovery visible among the charred hillside.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: But Jones described a rare ecosystem housing specialist plants, butterflies and insects, "where the UK is the epicentre globally".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "We've probably lost about 10 centimetres of soil here [at Sychnant Pass] so we've lost all of that organic matter layer... 4,000 years of carbon gone in a single event," he said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Once the topsoil is gone, we can never recover that.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "This soil acts as a water sponge, a carbon store, a nutrient bank.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Losing it is a double whammy, it worsens climate change and makes the habitat far more fragile." He added: "This site has taken thousands of years to develop and it's all gone in maybe five days?
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "If we are going to try and put that soil back, generate artificial soils through the reuse of organic wastes for example, then it's important we understand what the soil quality is now.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "So that we can prepare for the future and design those soils, because they don't exist yet." Over recent weeks the Bangor team has been racing to collect soil samples at several sites across Wales before heavy winter rainfall washes away the remains.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Their work has included comparing the burnt land with adjacent untouched areas, allowing researchers to measure changes in soil carbon, nutrients, microbial activity, water repellency and erosion risk.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Even NASA satellite data has been used to quickly identify new sites after fires have occurred.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Dr Kara Marsden says responding quickly is key Dr Kara Marsden, a lecturer in soil science who is also working on the project, said working at speed was vital.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It was really important that we got on site very quickly to measure the soil and vegetation properties while the fire's impacts were still fresh," she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "These things can change rapidly, so capturing that baseline data now means we'll have something accurate to compare against in future sampling dates." She warned that early green shoots now visible at the site did not necessarily reflect true or full recovery.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Bracken sprouts almost immediately because its rhizomes sit deep in the soil, so the burn layer wouldn't maybe have impacted those" she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "But the heather and gorse have much shallower roots, so you know they're completely gone.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "They've been completely lost... that depth of soil they depend on could take thousands of years to form again." Jones said that the impact of such wildfires extended far beyond biodiversity loss.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Fires release carbon, nitrogen and sulphur back into the atmosphere, in itself contributing to climate change," he said.

sentences.text: Alcohol buyers will be able to use a digital ID app on their phones to prove their age under new rules introduced on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Pubs and shops in England and Wales can use the tech in addition to current physical forms of ID - with the government saying a digital option will make age-checks quicker and more secure for customers and staff.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Customers will be able to choose ID apps from a range of suppliers such as the Post Office, Yoti or Luciditi, provided they are on a government-approved list.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The change means businesses will no longer be required to let people use physical ID, but the government contends most establishments would.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The plan will be technology-agnostic, meaning that the government is not setting out in detail how each app must work.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: It argues that under the voluntary digital ID scheme, drinkers would share fewer personal details with a venue or shop - such as tapping their phone on a reader or displaying a scannable QR code rather than handing over an official document.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The apps will also need to guard against customers borrowing devices from older friends and relatives, and ensure the ID app belongs to the person using it.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Yoti's digital ID app, for example, will only let a user log in if a scan of their face matches that of the person who signed up for the app.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The app then generates a QR code that can be scanned by a business with a free checker app, which tells them the person's age.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This is time-limited to make duping or sharing the QR code more difficult.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Digital government minister Stephanie Peacock said having the option for digital ID would "mean you do not need to carry a physical ID, nor hand over sensitive personal information" meaning people could "feel safer on a night out'".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Allen Simpson, chief executive of trade body UKHospitality, said the new rules were a "positive step".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: He added the industry would work with government to make sure the scheme's roll-out would not be "burdensome" for the hospitality sector.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This would include ensuring there were multiple options for suppliers and that it was cost-efficient, Simpson said.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...

sentences.text: "She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Europol tells the BBC the number of museum theft cases reported to them across Europe began to increase about two years ago.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Its recent report says both the methods and targets of thefts are changing - with a rise in more forceful tactics, and, as in the Louvre case, a focus on high-value items such as precious metals and gemstones.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Both Brand and Ibrahim Bulut, a museum security expert from a Belgian security consulting firm, believe many thefts that followed the Louvre burglary are copycats.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Every museum in the world is stressing now," Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Data provided to the BBC by ARCA shows recorded museum thefts in France spiked in 2024, and rose again slightly in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, numbers go up and down over time, with more thefts recorded in 2015 than a decade later.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Others point out the colonial history behind many treasures in European museums, with art historians highlighting the French crown jewels stolen from the Louvre contained emeralds, diamonds, sapphires and pearls which are not native to France.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are vulnerable and easy to burgle, Brand says, compared with well-secured jewellery shops and banks - which these days hold less cash.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Directors historically "never have enough money for security" or prefer to spend it on the next exhibition, and museums are often housed in old buildings that are difficult to protect, he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: For example, the Denis Diderot Maison des Lumières (House of Enlightenment) - burgled hours after the Louvre - is housed in two 18th-Century mansions in Langres.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We therefore have to reconcile modern security requirements with the need to preserve historic buildings and comply with France's heritage regulations," local mayor Théo Caviezel explains.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are also open public spaces that have less access control and perpetrators can come in as visitors, says Kumar Sokka, CEO of Acre Security which works with some museums in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: And even if a museum is secured well, thieves could still come in armed, Brand says, adding that it would be impractical to put police in galleries.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Many of these burglaries are over in minutes and the thieves have long gone by the time police show up - the Renoir case happened within five minutes.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Heists used to depend on deception, but burglaries are now becoming increasingly violent, Europol's report last month , external points out.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Offenders are using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives, to get inside.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Louvre, the thieves used a mechanical lift to gain access, cut through the window with power tools and then threatened guards, who left, before forcing their way inside displays and grabbing the jewels.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Renoir case, the perpetrators used an electric knife to cut through a fence before sawing through structures holding the paintings' frames in place.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The increased aggression creates new security concerns.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "An armed incident during opening hours, like the one we experienced, creates a situation in which the immediate priority is to keep our audience and staff safe," says Lilli Hollein, the director of the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) in Vienna, which was burgled last month.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Two people leave Louvre in lift mounted to vehicle What is being stolen is also changing.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: While paintings are still taken, they're harder to sell, so about 10 years ago, thieves began shifting to goods that are easier to get rid of, Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Now precious metals, gemstones, and culturally significant artefacts including Chinese porcelain are increasingly targeted, according to Europol's report.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process," it says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further." Meanwhile, Chinese porcelain is likely to be easily sold on the art market because of high demand, Europol says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After a theft, police generally have between four and six days to catch the thieves, according to Brand, who works with investigators by calling informants and receiving tips from the public or even ex-partners of perpetrators.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: But while suspects may be arrested, jewels or precious metals might not be found - such as with the Louvre case.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: On the other hand, Brand believes the Renoir paintings stolen this week - two of which were dropped by the thieves on their way out - "will probably be recovered" because "no one will want to buy" them and "it is likely, then, that the thieves have no idea what to do with them".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Christopher A Marinello, the boss of Art Recovery International that recovers stolen art, says only 5-10% of stolen art is ever recovered, making thefts from small museums like this week's "extra painful".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Tuesday's heist is another example of "Europe's museums under siege", he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After its theft in October, Maison des Lumières launched a security audit carried out by police officers appointed by France's cultural ministry, mayor Caviezel says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Some recommendations are already being implemented, such as enhanced video surveillance, while other structural improvements are in the process of being developed.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: MAK in Vienna also increased its security to prevent "copycat offenders and to provide our audience with visible security", its director says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Entry is through a metal detector, and bags must be put in the cloakroom or in lockers, and there are more security guards.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Experts say the trick is to create physical barriers that will delay thieves so there is time for the police to arrive, or to make any theft take so long that it would deter would-be offenders from attempting it.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Security is about buying time", says Bulut.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Sokka says it's critical to have integrated systems - so for example if an alarm goes off, you could shut down the facility, or lock down all high net worth paintings.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, security measures are expensive.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Mayor Caviezel, whose small French city hosts two museums and collections, says finding the money is "one of our main challenges".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A small city can be entrusted with collections of national importance without having the financial resources of a major Parisian institution." Bulut, who sits on the International Committee for Museum Security board, says it's not all about expensive gadgets.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: It could also be training guards to spot suspicious people who may be casing a museum and ask them if they need help, which may deter them from returning.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are investing: Sokka says his company has seen an uptick in seismic offerings, that can detect vibration such as drilling in walls, in the past 18 months.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museum heists are not increasing everywhere in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In Sweden, major museum thefts began to decline around a decade ago and have not changed significantly in recent years, said Peg Magnusson, Sweden's representative for a Unesco convention to combat illicit trafficking of cultural property.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, other worrying cultural artefact targets have emerged.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The challenge for museums now is increasing security while also staying open to the public.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A museum cannot be a fortress," Hollein says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We want to be open institutions; at the same time, we are facing new challenges and attacks against museums that will require new standards." Additional reporting by Madeleine Lake.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Laura Sarabia was Colombia's foreign minister from January to July 2025 Prosecutors in Colombia have accused former foreign minister Laura Sarabia of abusing her power after she made her nanny take a lie detector test.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: The scandal erupted in 2023, when Colombian news weekly Semana reported that a woman Sarabia had employed to look after her son had been hooked up to a polygraph and questioned over the alleged disappearance of a case full of cash from Sarabia's flat.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Sarabia, who was the chief of staff for President Gustavo Petro at the time, resigned in June 2023 but was later appointed as foreign minister and, following her resignation from that post, as Colombia's ambassador to the United Kingdom.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: She has denied any wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: The 32-year-old was one of the closest advisers of Gustavo Petro, Colombia's first left-wing president, who governed from 2022 to August this year.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Prosecutors said Sarabia abused her position as his chief of staff by ordering police to question her nanny, Marelbys Meza, over the alleged disappearance of the cash, which was said to amount to several thousands of dollars.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Meza told Semana that she was taken by Sarabia's driver to an official building opposite the presidential palace, saying it felt like "a kidnapping".
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Police officers then attached her to a polygraph machine and questioned her about the alleged disappearance of the money.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Meza denied having stolen any money during the test, and has consistently denied any wrongdoing in media interviews since.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that in ordering police to question Meza, Sarabia improperly used state resources to investigate a matter which was not related to her official post.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: Sarabia rejected the accusation during a hearing, without going into further details.
sentences.article_title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test

sentences.text: She had earlier said in a social media post that her lawyers were dealing with the issue and that she respected the judicial authorities and trusted their decisions.

sentences.text: Arturo Carrera Loaiza has denied allegations that he was involved in methamphetamine production, Nigeria's drugs control authority says An alleged Mexican drug kingpin was arrested in Nigeria last month as he tried to leave the country, the drug enforcement authority has just revealed.
